Positron annihilation sites vs a Gaussian random walk

Monte Carlo of positrons from a point source in a uniform medium (continuous slowing-down + multiple scattering), compared with a 2D Gaussian of matched width.

Projection onto the x–y plane of the annihilation positions for a point source at the origin. Both panels use the same number of events, field of view and colour scale. The positron distribution is sharply cusped with long tails; the matched Gaussian is much flatter-topped and has almost no tail.

Solid lines with markers: Monte Carlo samples. Dashed: analytic 2D Gaussian with the matched σ. (a) is the probability per unit area, so ∫ρ 2πr dr = 1.

Summary statistics

Model and caveats

  • Kinetic energy is drawn from an allowed β⁺ spectrum with a Fermi-function correction (single branch, Eₘₐₓ only; the real ⁶⁸Ga and ⁸²Rb spectra have additional branches).
  • Each positron loses energy along the Katz–Penfold CSDA range–energy relation for water (fit valid 0.01–2.5 MeV; extrapolated for ⁸²Rb), with direction changes from a Highland-type multiple-scattering angle at every step. It annihilates at rest when its energy falls below 1 keV; in-flight annihilation, non-collinearity and positronium formation are ignored.
  • Density only rescales distances (range ∝ 1/ρ), which ignores differences in Z/A between tissues.
  • "Gaussian random walk" here means a 2D isotropic Gaussian centred on the source, with σ per axis chosen by the matching option. This is a quick physical model, not a substitute for a full Geant4/GATE or PeneloPET simulation.
